kyler: Heads-up — seeing a small-batch (bs=2) regression where KV hits drop dramatically compared to bs=8. Can someone capture an nsys + torch.profiler sample for the repro? Want a flamegraph + profiler table to compare.

maria: I can take this. any preferred env / cmd? :+1:

kyler: Thanks. Repro script is tools/repro/run_small_batch.sh — run on rtx-a100-48G if possible. Capture both: nsys for kernel timelines and torch.profiler for op-level stacks. Example nsys command: ```nsys profile --output=/tmp/trace_ns --force --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=cpu --stats=true --duration=60s python tools/repro/run_small_batch.py --batch-size 2``` Also run with TORCH_PROFILER context in the script: ```with torch.profiler.profile(..., profile_memory=True, record_shapes=True) as prof: ... prof.export_chrome_trace('/tmp/torchprof.json')```

alex: Cool. I'll run this on shard-4 in ~30m. Do we need to scrub anything before upload?

kyler: Yes — remove any customer prompt texts and API keys. Use scripts/scrub_trace.py for torch traces and scripts/scrub_nsys.sh for nsys metadata. Also include env dump: `env | grep -E "(AWS|S3|REDWOOD|HTTP|API)"` and `pip freeze > /tmp/requirements.txt` (or `conda list`).

perf-bot: auto-note: capture slot allocated on shard-4 (node-id: node-97). please upload to s3://redwood-perf/traces/1915000000/ within 24h or the slot will be released.

maria: Ran into huge .nvtrace size (8GB). Compressed to .nsz with `nsys export` and then gz. Uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/traces/1915000000/maria_ns.nsz.gz and s3://redwood-perf/traces/1915000000/maria_torch.json.gz. Posted presigned URLs to #eng-runtime-private.

kyler: Thanks — can you also paste the exact command you used to compress? and confirm you ran with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0 (we want async behavior).

maria: Command: `nsys export -i /tmp/trace_ns.qdrep -o /tmp/trace_ns --type=nsz && gzip /tmp/trace_ns.nsz` and `gzip /tmp/torchprof.json`. CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING unset (so default async).

alex: Quick ask: when you captured, did you pin threads? we saw different scheduling causing weird kernel interleaving last time. For reproducibility add `taskset -c 0-7` around the run.

maria: good call — I'll rerun with pinned CPUs and collect a 30s focused trace.

kyler: For analysis, please include a small sample log snippet (stdout/stderr) with the exact model commit hash and the server git branch. Also include `python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))"` output.

maria: Uploaded second set: s3://redwood-perf/traces/1915000000/maria_ns_pinned.nsz.gz and maria_torch_pinned.json.gz. Logs: s3://redwood-perf/traces/1915000000/maria_logs.txt

infra-bot: reminder: presigned URLs expire in 7 days. Consider moving to perf-archive if you need long-term storage.

kyler: I'll take the pinned traces and run the flamegraph diff. If I see KV cache miss skew, I'll open a mini-bisect and tag the problematic commit in the thread. Thanks all. :rocket:
